name: Glaciated Scramble (Standard)
approach: From the Blanca Lake Trailhead (elev. ~1,950 ft) at the end of North Fork Skykomish River Road (FR 63), follow Blanca Lake Trail #1052 north into the Henry M. Jackson Wilderness. The trail starts climbing almost immediately in a long, punishing series of roughly thirty switchbacks, gaining about 2,900 ft over the first ~3 miles to a ridge crest — this is the steepest, most sustained grind of the whole approach, and can be muddy, rooty, and icy in wet or early-season conditions (microspikes worth carrying outside of high summer). From the ridge the trail rolls on through meadows to Virgin Lake (~4,600 ft, roughly mile 3.5), the high point of the trail; the main tread then drops about 600 ft to Blanca Lake, a good camp for an overnight approach and the last easy, reliable water source before the off-trail climbing begins. At Virgin Lake, do NOT continue downhill on the main tread toward Blanca Lake — that is the single most common route-finding error here. Instead pick up the faint, unsigned climbers' path leaving the lake into the woods toward Kyes Ridge. This boot path gains Kyes Peak's south ridge and follows it northeast, staying on the ridge's east side to traverse around minor gendarmes; it levels out near 5,300 ft, crosses to the west side around 5,845 ft, then climbs steep heather and scree above, working around cliff bands. A boulder field near 6,300 ft leads to a notch by Point 7026, from which class 3-4 scrambling on so-so Monte Cristo-group rock gains the summit ridge and final block. Total elevation gain from trailhead to the 7,282-ft high point is roughly 6,000 ft over about 6-7 miles one-way (12-14 miles round trip) — this is a long single push with a likely-after-dark return, or better done as an overnight camped at Virgin Lake. An alternative approach/ascent line climbs the Columbia Glacier out of the Blanca Lake basin (low-angled but genuinely crevassed — rope, axe, and crampons are the safe call even though some parties skip them in low-snow years) and gains the upper mountain from the north; several trip reports pair this glacier line for the ascent with the south-ridge climbers' trail for the descent, or the reverse.

pitch_detail.notes: Ridge and boulder-field scrambling above the northeast base; mostly Class 2 with short Class 3 steps
pitch_detail.pitch: Ridge/boulder scramble (~6,600 ft to summit block)

pitch_detail.notes: Short, exposed, notably loose/chossy final scramble to the true summit; some parties sling a hand-line
